units.name: Economics, Supply Chain Management and Marketing Department
units.evidence: Current School of Business page explicitly names the combined department. Its BBA concentration description establishes substantive management of production/delivery resources, inventory planning/control, purchasing, transport and warehousing. Supply Chain Management is a concentration, not a standalone department.

decisions.reason: Imported Supply Chain Management label is a BBA concentration. The current official combined Economics, Supply Chain Management and Marketing Department is retained with its exact school host, rather than inventing a standalone SCM department.

sources.note: Read full current School of Business page, degree inventory, all named department contact/directory links and institutional footer. Explicit Economics, Supply Chain Management and Marketing Department. Graduate articulation agreements are awards at other institutions.

Read full visible Business Administration page and expanded Supply chain management concentration. Explicit BBA concentration, resource/activity management producing/delivering goods/services, inventory planning/control, purchasing, transport and warehousing. Named department contact confirms actual combined unit. Other concentration panels not expanded.
Read entire first unfiltered academic inventory page, all degree types and entries, then followed visible pagination.

Read entire second unfiltered inventory page. Engineering is an undergraduate transfer pathway, supply-chain analytics is an external Clayton State master’s articulation, and professional doctorates described are external partner awards.

Read final unfiltered inventory page, last four entries and final pagination. Current direct Master of Arts in Teaching is listed, despite footer describing a bachelor-degree-granting institution; no current direct doctorate appears across all three pages.

limitations: Full current degree inventory includes a direct Teaching master’s, despite a generic bachelor-degree-granting footer. The inventory governs doctoral review. External articulation agreements do not establish direct institutional doctoral awards.
